I might, instead of taking it personally, reflect on the fact that the person criticizing me is actually talking about themselves. This allows me to deal with criticism with a bit less anger, and a lot more compassion.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My crush flirts with me a lot, talks to me everyday, etc., but he told his friends that he doesn’t want anything serious (without telling me about it). I feel kind of betrayed. What should I do?
Answer: Clear communication is a superpower. It makes everything better, in particular my relationships. The very opposite of clear communication sounds something like: he told them, and they told me, but he didn’t tell me, and now I’m hurt. It creates a convoluted line where there should be a straight line. It creates pain and betrayal that came out of what may be just a fog. Whenever I see a long, convoluted line, I shorten and straighten it. I do this by communicating directly to the person I am wondering about. If I talk to someone every day, on any one of those days I say: we’re flirting and talking and I want to tell you something. I am not just fooling around. I really like you. What I want to do is spend time with people who want the same thing I want. What I want to do is set the tone for how we communicate in the future - not by him telling them and then telling me and me doubting and wondering - but in us building intimacy and trust by talking directly to each other. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do you make a girl love you a lot while you are in a friendship?
Answer: First step: forget about trying to “make a girl love you” and focus instead on being true to who you are, what you like and what you want. Trying to “make someone love me” accounts for most of the stupid shit I’ve done that I’ve regretted. Second: be clear about your intentions. “I know we’re friends, but I really like you.” I cannot tell you the number of times someone liked me back and we were a mess because we weren’t clear with each other. Third: she will either like you back, or she won’t. But if she does, she will like you for exactly who you are, instead of liking that person who tried to make her love you, who wasn’t really you. You will discard these steps now but realize over the years they were written with the intent of saving you a lot of time and immeasurable heartbreak.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Why does my partner not ask me questions about myself anymore?
Answer: Sometimes, (often), we have no way of knowing the answer to a question, we jump to the conclusion that we know. We give you answers that come from our own experience, with other people or with ourselves. So, you might get answers like “your partner doesn’t ask you questions about you because they don’t love you anymore.” Or, “because they are hurt.” Or, Or “because they are totally self-involved.” These answers may be true for the people who write them, but they are in no way connected to you or your partner, because we don’t know them, and we don’t know you. This point is more important than any of us can imagine and goes way beyond this question, because it’s about the tools we use to design our life. Should we be taking advice from people who are having their experience but are not having ours? Should we be asking questions to people who are guaranteed to have answers, but answers unrelated to what we are asking? Should we see a projection, an assumption or a guess as fact, or even as helpful? The right question to the right person is a treasure. But the wrong question, or the right question to the wrong people, is a red herring, us setting off on a fool’s errand, us, deliberately misleading ourselves.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How would someone emotionally manipulate you?
Answer: By getting really close really fast. I’ve never felt this way before. By not owning what they do or say. Wow. Slow your roll. I was just kidding. By lying. I was at the gym. By making you feel guilty. You would if you loved me. By using ultimatums. If you do that, I’m out. By using how you feel or what you say against you. By taking advantage of you. By making excuses. By blaming you. By altering the truth. By disclosing only parts of what happened. By making you doubt yourself. By diminishing your concerns. By overwhelming you. By intimidating you. By threatening you. By blackmailing you. By rushing you. By surprising you. By going silent. By putting you down. The logic is that the smaller your self worth, the easier you are to manipulate.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What is an emotionally abusive girlfriend?
Answer: Are they making you doubt yourself, denying that something took place (when it did), making you believe that how you perceive things is not accurate? Wow. You are making a mountain out of a molehill. A storm in a glass of water. I never said that. You are so sensitive. Do you feel like you are being cut off from the people that you love? I don’t like your friends. We see your family too much. Do they say hurtful, diminishing, insulting things? Do you feel your sense of self-worth is being sabotaged? I don’t think you will ever accomplish that. I don’t think it’s in you to finish that project. Is blame being shifted? The problem is you. I would not be so exasperated if you weren’t late all the time. Our conversations would be better if you stopped arguing with me. Do they raise their voice, are they getting right in your face, being aggressive and loud? Is their behavior controlling or jealous? Jealousy is not a sign of love. It’s a sign of abuse. You can’t wear that. That person cannot be your friend. I am certain you are cheating on me. Is their behavior violent? They break things, slam their hand on the table, punch things, throw things. And, notice how you are feeling. Are you afraid of making a mistake? Do you feel nervous? Are you walking on eggshells? You are not supposed to be afraid of someone you love.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I draw the line between being emotionally abusive and really trying to make my relationship work better?
Answer: No. Look. Trying to make my relationship better works like this: I am loving. I am kind. I am generous. I pay attention. If the person I love is trying to connect with me, I respond. I make my relationship a priority. I communicate as clearly as I can. This includes listening intently. This means voicing expectations, and asking instead of assuming. I set boundaries, and respect the boundaries they set. I show appreciation, instead of finding things to criticize. You are wonderful. I love you. Thank you. Being emotionally abusive looks like this: I am disrespectful. I am cruel. I refuse to listen. I gaslight. I make someone else doubt what they are perceiving. Instead of communicating, I give them the silent treatment. I control. I threaten. I use ultimatums. I criticize everything. I put the other person down. It’s lethal to assume that treating another person poorly is in any way constructive or will somehow result in a better relationship.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How can I make my dad proud?
Answer: Stop thinking about what you could do to make your dad proud and start exploring what it is that you want. Orienting your life towards what someone else wants for you is the quickest way to feel lost, listless and disconnected. Set aside anything your dad has ever said about you and decide for yourself who you really are and where you want to go. Embark on your own life. Ask no one for advice so that you learn to both listen and trust your own decisions. Sometimes your decisions will be wrong. Don’t confuse that with incompetence - being wrong sometimes is just a part of being human. Realize that parents see themselves in their children but their children - you, and me - are more than a wavering reflection of the people who made us. We are our own people and our most sacred assignment is to claim this life that we were given. It is ours. It is not theirs. Realize that whatever your dad - or anyone - feels about you is less about you and more about how he feels about himself. This is really difficult to internalize but your dad’s dismay is him looking at his life, not him looking at you. Go forge your own life that he will one day realize is glorious because it’s all yours rather than something that vaguely reminds him of all the things he did not accomplish in his. That is how you make someone proud. Or, maybe making him proud can’t be done. Maybe he is broken and lacks the ability to feel pride but at that point his opinions about you will matter to you a lot less than what you think about yourself. Living a life you can be proud of is the only antidote to the hopelessness of living a life attempting to please people who cannot be pleased.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Why do some people agree to donate their body organs after they die?
Answer: Imagine that I am in possession of something so valuable that it has the ability to save somebody’s life, or completely change it for the better. This item is vital to me too, but one day circumstances are such that I am no longer going to need it. So, the options are: For this unspeakably valuable item to go to waste; or For it to be put in the hands of a person who needs it to survive. Why would I let it go to waste?

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What if you had a disagreement with your partner. how long would you not talk to him for?
Answer: Let me tell you what to me is the foundation of a healthy, committed relationship in the most simple, bare-bones terms. Our behavior, our actions and words all converge in a single message: you are safe with me. If I do things that scare you, that make you doubt my commitment, that make you feel that I threaten you or put you at risk, that relationship is crumbling. If we get into a disagreement and you decide not to talk to me, that would scare me. It would frustrate me. I would feel…unsafe. You deciding not to talk to me would leave me without an opportunity to come together and resolve our disagreement. You leave me without recourse. Deciding not to talk to me shows an absence of communication skills. It’s a form of emotional withdrawal that will destroy every healthy relationship. See, we had a fight and instead of reassuring each other you left me out in the cold.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What is a common piece of "good advice" given to young adults that you actually think is terrible life advice, and why?
Answer: I will give you three: Never go to bed angry. This is a recipe for feeling overextended and overwhelmed. Instead - pause. Take a break. Go to bed. Things will look better in the morning. Communication is better with a fresh, rested, clear-eyed perspective. Never give up. A recipe for burnout and hopelessness. Many times, giving up is better than holding on to something that is not working. Cut your loses. Put your energy into more fruitful pursuits. You only live once. This justifies making terrible decisions. You have one life, and through it you live with the decisions that you make. Make them count.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do you explain to your bf that you need him to be there emotionally for you?
Answer: If someone said to me “I need you to be there emotionally for me” I would consider this statement somewhat abstract. I would ask “can you tell me what this looks like to you?” If I wanted someone to be there emotionally for me, I might make very specific requests. For example: “I want to talk through something with you. Do you think I can have about 15 minutes of your full attention?” Or I might say “I am doubting my own experience of something and I wonder if I can tell you about it and have you tell me what you think - to validate me, or to disagree.” Or “I have a doctor appointment that makes me nervous and I wonder if you can come with me”. Or even “can you please hold me while I cry without asking me not to cry?” When someone needs something from me, I ask for specific examples, and try to give specific examples in return.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I discern what part of me is real vs. the facade I put out?
Answer: Façade: uneasy, fearful, a sense of disconnection, feeling listless, struggling with low self esteem and a lack of self confidence. I don’t know what I can do. I don’t know if I can trust myself. I don't know how I feel. I don’t know me. I am just going through the motions. I wonder what’s real. Me: confident, hungry to try new things, alive, flawed, empowered, connected, inspired, purpose-driven, clear, peaceful. I know who I am and what I can do. It’s OK if I try something unsuccessfully - I can try again. It’s OK if this is hard. I trust that I am capable.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: When I am with my boyfriend, he always looks at other women in front of me and stares at them at time. Why?
Answer: When I am with my partner (and OK also when I am not with my partner), I look at other women. I look at other men too. I do this walking down the street but I also do it when I am watching a movie or a reel or a show. Ooooh. Look at him. Hawt. I do this because I am human, and am drawn to things my eyes consider beautiful. None of this - even the flutter I feel when I am attracted to someone - threatens my commitment to my partner. My partner is also very pulled in by beauty. I find this delightful because beauty is uplifting and available to us everywhere. Why would I attempt to deprive him of something so lovely and plentiful? Life is hard enough. I don’t think his hungry, roving eyes affect me. There will always be women (and men) more beautiful than me, and even this does not impact the solidity of our relationship. How controlling would we need to be to want to restrain what the other glances at? As long as looking at beautiful things is done respectfully, as long as there is self-confidence and trust, I’ve decided to set myself free from attempting to contain something so natural, so healthy and so life affirming.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My boyfriend said he wouldn’t care if I passed and doesn’t feel the need to do absolutely anything for me ever. Says I deserve nothing. If he hates me so much why doesn’t he leave?
Answer: Look. People are inexplicable and do and say inexplicable things. I could spend the rest of my life wondering why on earth they do what they do. Except, the answers would never come, because we can’t possibly know. So, whenever I ask myself questions about other people that I cannot possibly answer, I turn the question back to me. Why Dushka? Why are you giving your time and energy to someone who says you deserve nothing?

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: If my boyfriend gets drunk and starts flirting with other girls, is that the alcohol coercing him to do it or is it his internal thoughts coming through? Should I still be with him if he does it?
Answer: Two of the most important ingredients in a healthy relationship are trust, and accountability. The person I am in a relationship with and I need to be able to trust each other. And, we both need to be fully responsible for our actions. If someone behaves inappropriately when they drink, to me it doesn’t matter if it’s the alcohol or their inner thoughts. To me what matters is: is this person taking responsibility, or blaming alcohol for their behavior? And, are they someone I can trust? (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Which of your books would you recommend for a friend with major depressive disorder? He is seeking mental health treatment. However, I want to give him an additional/personal boost towards his well being.
Answer: I want to start by making clear what you already suggest in your question: my books are not a cure or a treatment for depression. I am so glad your friend is already seeking treatment. That being said, these are a few books he might enjoy: How to be ferociously happy and other essays. Feelings are fickle and other things I wish someone had told me. The love of our life is you (this is a workbook - so if you give him this book, include a blank notebook for a really nice touch.) For all I know: a shebang of checklists for life. All of my books are comprised of one page essays, so they don’t feel overwhelming to read. Thank you for asking about my books. And, you can find a full list here:

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What is the difference between knowing something and having a hunch?
Answer: If I know something, I am cognizant of it. If I have a hunch, I suspect it. These two are very different. Knowing is related to fact. A hunch is related to instinct.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Who or what is your Quora avatar, and why did you choose it?
Answer: My Quora avatar is an image of me, hand drawn by Dan Roam. I chose it because I feel the drawing (like many of his drawings) captured something ineffable that feels like me. Dan frequently illustrates my answers with drawings that most of the time take him less than two or three minutes. He also has designed the covers for my last five books (which you can see if you click on my name and go to my profile page.) He has written many books about visual storytelling and visual thinking. You can learn more about him at DIGITAL ROAM INC. I adore his work. I think he is extremely talented.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Isn’t triage in an emergency room some sort of discrimination? Why is it legal?
Answer: Once, many years ago, the man I was married to clutched his chest and told me he felt “a terrible pressure”. I insisted for hours that we go to the hospital, to which he said “no, this will pass in a moment.” When I finally convinced him, just to rule out the possibility of something serious, we both jaunted into the emergency room looking like two people ready to go to the movies. There was nothing visibly wrong with either of us. We spoke to the nurse, who asked a few questions and rushed him in, in front of many people who were already waiting. The pressure in his chest had in fact been a heart attack, and he had two more while in the hospital. He now has a stent in his heart. Triage is a selection process by which the emergency room staff determines who needs to be seen first. If you are very lucky, triage will have you waiting for hours. If you are also very lucky, one day it will save your life. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Can being single for a long time change a person?
Answer: Yes, of course. Being single for a long time definitely changes a person, just like being in a relationship for a long time changes a person. Being single can make me more isolated, more in-my-head, more lonely, more set in my ways, more anxious and more depressed. Or, being single can contribute to me getting to know myself better, can make me more self-reliant, independent, selective, mindful, more prone to exploring my own interests. Being single can make me more resilient and over time less interested in a relationship. Over time, it can also make me more interested in a relationship. Experiences change us - and, an experience is not the only variable in determining the impact it has on us.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: When someone "needs a moment", why does that person often feel better after having that moment?
Answer: I don’t need to immediately react. “Taking a moment” will improve my choices, my decisions and my relationships. In that moment, connect to myself so I can hear me. I connect to myself so I can soothe me. I connect with myself so I can evaluate. I collect myself. I take deep breaths. I reboot. I go from “I cannot do this” to “I am listening.” A moment separates action from reaction. It takes me from impulse to consideration. It takes me from emotional to thoughtful. I go from overwhelmed to settled. I go from jumbled to gaining perspective. Take it. Take a moment. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I know if I am successful or unsuccessful?
Answer: Success is up to me to define. Here are some questions I find helpful in determining if I am successful or not: Do I do a bit each day that will eventually get me where I want to go? Do I stick to what I am good at, or am I OK feeling over my head sometimes? In situations that normally stress me out, do I feel…better than I once did? Am I able to manage my emotions? Do I follow through on what I say I am going to do? What motivates my decisions - the way they impact me, or impressing others? Do I feel the need to manage what others think of me? Do I feel comfortable changing my mind? Am I more open, more receptive? Am I free from grudges? Are my relationships loving and supportive? Am I able to “do nothing” without feeling guilty? Do I treat myself with compassion? Do I consider myself to be on my side? Do I in some way put what I do in the service of others?

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I end a relationship with my girlfriend of 5 years without hurting her?
Answer: I don’t think it’s possible to avoid hurting someone when you break up with them. But I do think there are good and bad ways to handle a break up. Let’s start with things you should not do. Please don’t break up with someone via text. Don’t attack, criticize or blame. Don’t say “I want to be your friend” unless you really mean it. Don’t be ambiguous or confusing. Don’t say “I am here if you need to talk.” What they need to recover from is you. Things you should do: Be kind. Be generous. Be direct. Be honest. Be brief. Pick a place that is somewhat private to give you both a chance be emotional: angry, sad or teary. Be very explicit about the good things they did for you. “Thank you for teaching me to believe in myself” or even “thank you for loving me”. Make it clean. No confusing language. Don’t call it “a break” or say you “need space” or leave room for the other person to wonder if they need to “wait” for you. During a break up, a lack of clarity is a form of cruelty.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What did you do to your hair that you will never do again?
Answer: I’ve never done anything to my hair: I’ve never straightened it, colored it, permed it or done anything to it other than have someone cut it. Except. There was a very unfortunate episode where a friend convinced me to highlight it. I hated everything about it: the feeling of being closely assessed, the sense that there was something wrong about the natural color of my hair (ugh this is so…flat!), the yanking, the smell of chemicals and the result. It just didn’t work for me. It took a long time to grow out. Since that time, I let my hair do whatever she wants: curl, puff, bounce, become grey. You do you, hair. I like you no matter what.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I hurt my girlfriend badly and she said that her feelings for me have changed. What should I do to get everything back as it was?
Answer: When we enter a relationship we create an ecosystem with its own chemistry and equilibrium. Hurting someone badly, or getting hurt, alters its composition forever. Put simply, things will never go back to the way they were. There are two possible outcomes: The first: The relationship does not survive. The second: we accept that we need to begin again and work hard at creating a new ecosystem. Over time we establish a new equilibrium, find ourselves in a relationship that is not what it used to be but that can be better, deeper, and more rewarding.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I really don't feel like I deserve love. How do you come to love yourself?
Answer: I don’t think arriving at loving myself came from “feeling love” or from feeling I deserved love. This is probably because it’s hard to love a stranger. Loving myself came instead from going through painful things and making them more painful for myself and deciding one day that I’d had enough. Perceiving the world through my insecurities - comparing myself to others, striving to get everything perfect and assuming at every turn that I was not good enough - was becoming exhausting. Putting effort into being likable instead of on figuring out what I wanted felt like I was getting further and further away from understanding who I was. Why am I working so hard at getting people to like me? I don't even know if I like them. Who even are they? Spending more time not communicating (such as playing hard to get or pretending I was interested in things I was not interested in), instead of learning how to communicate clearly, was getting me the very opposite of what I was after. Treating myself poorly, as if I was the enemy - why do I suck? Why do I always do this? Why can’t I ever learn? - was crushing me. Berating myself never worked, so maybe it was time to try something that would: Patience. Compassion. Understanding. Slowly, over time, I began treating myself like someone who was on my side. Like someone I could count on. Like someone who would never leave me. As I followed through on what I said I was going to do I learned, just by watching me, that I was worthy of my own trust. I stopped spending time with people who were not good for me, stopped comparing myself to others, and gave up on getting things perfect. I started expressing what I wanted, and setting boundaries to protect myself from feeling overwhelmed, taken advantage of or resentful. I began nurturing my loving relationships. People who felt about me the way I felt about them. No more trying to convince someone to love me. No more compromising myself to keep the peace. I became adamant about making my own decisions. No more handing over to others the very thing that gave shape to my existence: my choices. Over time I became what I had always been: the boss of my own life. All this is a process and took a long time and I still have good days and bad days. It’s not a switch. Self love is not a feeling. It’s a discipline, a way to live related to self-awareness, that results in life being a little bit easier. I am a flawed person - I don’t love me because I’m perfect. I love me because I am me, and feel that for this reason I deserve my care, my dedication, and my resources. I love me because in the trench we call life, I can’t be at war with the one person in here with me. Over time I’ve come to like me a lot, and this feeling has made life less painful. And that’s how I came to love myself.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I swim two miles a day. My buddy says I’m not really swimming because I use a snorkel. What do you say?
Answer: If you are disciplined, if you find something worth sticking to, if it contributes to your sanity, your health and your overall well being, if it grants you a measure of joy - well. You’ve hit the jackpot, my friend. And. Once you’ve hit the jackpot, so many people around you will gather around and say so much stupid stuff. I don't understand why you do this. You are not doing it right. How are you going to “monetize” it? It would be better if you did it this other way. You do this every day? Wow. Aren’t you wasting your time? What do I say? Pay them no mind. Swim. Swim! Move your body and listen to the rhythm of your breath and know that there, in the water, with your snorkel, you have everything. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I distinguish between reconciliation and forgiveness? Is it possible to forgive someone but not reconcile with him or her?
Answer: Reconciliation: let’s agree to end the hostility we have towards one another. Let’s accept that something painful happened and find a way to move on. Reconciliation may imply giving the relationship another chance, perhaps in a different form to what it once had. Forgiveness is: I wish you no ill will. I feel no resentment towards you. Forgiveness is for me, so I can live without poison in my heart. You can absolutely say “I forgive you, but no longer want you in my life.”

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do you play hard to get?
Answer: Playing hard to get means acting like I am not interested in an attempt to make another person interested in me. This means acting counter to what I want. (I want you, ergo I will act distant and aloof.) Clarity is one of my favorite things and playing hard to get is the very opposite - but this is not the worst part. The worst part is that playing hard to get guarantees I will attract the wrong people. Here is how it works: If I tell a person that I am interested in them, and they are interested in me, this will come as great news to them. If I tell a person that I am not interested, and this makes them more interested in me, it means they enjoy breaking boundaries. They hear “no” and want to push harder. I end up with people with a tendency to not listen when I say no, people who are overly possessive and controlling, who want a conquest, to own me, rather than to love me. If I say what I want really clearly “I really like you and would love to see you again” and this makes that person lose interest, then that person is not for me.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What are people's opinions on "The Third Life" by Dushka Zapata?
Answer: Hello! I am Dushka Zapata, and I have never written a book titled “The Third Life”. If you want to take a look at the books I have in fact written, you can find a comprehensive list here: I will soon be editing this list to add a book I am currently struggling with. Why am I struggling with it? Mostly because I am really busy at my job and have very little time left (not to mention, the emotional brain-space needed to think about what I am doing.) My hope is to have it ready in early December.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What makes a girl/woman instantly unattractive?
Answer: Treating someone like you are somehow superior, like they are less than you, being disrespectful by putting them down, is unbecoming to everyone. This looks like making fun of someone, making a joke at someone’s expense, sneering, mimicking, saying something sarcastic or intentionally insensitive, fighting and twisting the argument to make the other person look incompetent or incapable. This behavior is pretty universal: we’ve all done it to others, and we’ve all been a victim of it, so I watch myself closely in an effort to strike it out of my life. There are so many ways to communicate better and more effectively. I think contempt makes anyone, of any gender, instantly unattractive.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What are the challenges you are facing currently on your books?
Answer: I love to write and writing a book involves things other than writing. The first part is related to assembling the book. What is it about? What do I want to say? Do I think that what I am saying will be something others can put to use if they want to? Regarding editing and curating, how can I structure it? What should stay? What should go? What would make a good title? What should the cover look like? I am looking over a pile of things I’ve already written, and I feel like this is taking away from time I could be writing new things. (I am so grateful Melissa Hoy helps me collect and organize my Quora answers.) The second part is related to selling the book. I am terrible at self-promotion and don’t spend any time at all marketing my books. Is there something I should be doing to give them a chance to be read by more people, to sell better? What would that look like? If you read one of my books and like it and write a review and share the book on social media, I am deeply grateful because you are doing for my book all the marketing I am doing for my books. Here again I feel that time spent marketing is time I am not spending writing. The challenge I face with my books is anything related to writing a book that has nothing to do with writing.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Why can’t men be more direct and just tell you they just want to be friends, instead of playing with females’ feelings?
Answer: Learning to communicate clearly is really, really hard - quite possibly the challenge of a lifetime, the challenge that threads itself across every action we ever take. Clear communication takes a lot of practice, a lot of skill, a lot of empathy and a lot of emotional maturity. Even people with decades of experience bumble, fumble, make mistakes and miss the mark. We make mistakes because we want things to be easy and try to take the shortcut, because we want what we want but also want to avoid hurting others; because we are clumsy, or because we look at things the way we want them to be instead of the way they are. I don’t think unclear communication is a men problem (or a women problem). I think it’s a human problem. I think that the solution is to learn. To develop an ability to be direct and honest and compassionate, all at the same time. It’s a tall order. Of course sometimes people (regardless of gender) play with other people’s feelings. But, most of the time, when it comes to clear communication, we are all rookies, and make rookie mistakes.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: To women, why do you sometimes hate when a guy approaches you respectfully, compliments you and asks for your number? Wouldn't that be a welcome experience, even though you reject/don't like the guy?
Answer: If a guy approached me, complimented me and asked for my number, I wouldn’t feel hatred. What I’d feel is fear. I’d feel exactly the way you would feel if a guy approached you, complimented you and asked for your number. (What? Is this a scam? Why does this person who doesn’t know me generically compliment me and ask for my phone number!?) If a stranger pays me a compliment and asks for my number, the compliment comes with an agenda. It’s not given freely - it’s an instrument of manipulation. I am flattering you because I want something. It’s a socially acceptable way to test and push on boundaries. It can feel like someone is setting up some kind of trap around me. I don’t know this guy at all. Am I in a position where I can reject him without personal risk? Does saying no compromise my safety? Does it put me in an awkward place in any way? If so, the guy is thinking about what he wants but not thinking about the position he is putting me in. How is the guy going to respond if I don’t react the way that he wants me to? Will he be indignant that I did not consider his invasive act a welcome experience? Will he be hurtful, act like I am being ungrateful, act like I need to act flattered, like he is giving me a desirable experience when really I am just wondering how much danger I am in? When it comes to meeting new people, the first thing we need to ask ourselves is: am I making this person feel like a mark? Is anything I am doing making them feel like prey? And, am I giving them an easy way to decline my advances?

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My boyfriend says he loves me but he’s not happy with me. How do I save my relationship?
Answer: If my boyfriend said he loved me but what not happy with me, I would ask him to sit down with me and tell me more. What are the things he is not happy with? If the things he is not happy with point to behavior I need to change because it will make me better and in the long run contribute to me suffering less, I put into practice the ability that I have to change. Not for him - or not only for him - but for myself. Love has a way of making us grow that can be daunting and painful but ultimately rewarding and beautiful. If the things he is not happy with point to something essential in me, important to me, or mean that I have to in some way compromise myself, I deduce we are not compatible. I understand you are not happy with me and I think you have to find someone you can be happy with because the person you want is not who I am.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: If my mother is arguing with a neighbor and she is not right, should I support her even if she is not right, or should I be impartial and withdraw my mother from the discussion?
Answer: If someone I love is having an argument and is in the wrong, there is one thing I owe them, out of the respect, trust and love that I feel for them: the truth. I say “I think you are wrong, and this is why.” I don’t think it’s my job to get involved in the argument, join in on the argument or “withdraw” them from the argument. In this love I feel for them, I trust that they are capable. I trust they can manage their own argument. I don't need to “help” them. But, in a private moment, I do tell them what I think, not because I am not supportive or loyal, but because I am.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My husband, during arguments, always calls me ignorant. Is it an angry word?
Answer: I am so sorry your husband does this. It sounds so painful and diminishing. Calling someone ignorant is very disrespectful and mocking. The intent is to make the person feel small. It also assumes an attitude of superiority: clearly, I am better than you. Contempt is so hurtful and so damaging that it weakens our immune system. According to The Gottman Institute, contempt is the single greatest predictor of divorce. There are ways to change the course of contempt. Here are a few: To begin conversations with how something makes you feel, instead of talking about the other person. Something like: I feel lonely and need to spend more time with you. Can we talk about it? Instead of: you are so careless! You can’t even see what you are doing to me! In the long term, the antidote to contempt is to build a culture of admiration within your relationship. Can you praise instead of nag? Can you say thank you out loud? Can you kiss more frequently? Can you replace complaining with admiring? I think treating someone with contempt is common and (ironically, given your question) comes from ignorance. We simply don’t know the tools to create better relationships - learning them truly improves them. I recommend you read more about The Gottman Institute, specifically what they write about the behaviors that destroy relationships. They are very easy to Google but here is a good article to get you started: Needless to say, I do not work for them or represent them in any way. I am just someone who has benefited greatly from the work they do. My hope is that you do too.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: He is not sure about our future relationship, but he doesn't want me to leave his life. What does that mean?
Answer: It means that I am giving so much time and energy to their ambivalence and uncertainty that I am neglecting to turn this time and energy back to me. Setting aside the quandary of what he is feeling, what do I want? What do I want my future to look like? Do I want someone who feels ambiguity about our relationship? Do I want someone completely unpredictable who makes me feel bewildered and mystified rather than safe? Or do I want someone who is as sure about me as I am about them? What it means is that I get to decide what I want for myself, and leave behind anyone who is not compatible with what I want. Not because I don’t love them, but because I love me. I am sorry you are not sure, my love. My wish for you is that you go find what you seek. You need to leave my life so I can make room for someone certain about me. It’s time to give ourselves the future we deserve. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: After 34 years, my husband says he’s not in love with me, and still wants me. I’m so confused at what kind of relationship I am in. What should I do?
Answer: Whenever I am in a relationship that confuses me, I remind myself of one undeniable thing that is easy to forget: the “relationship” is not something mysterious I am in. It’s not something that happens to me. rather, I AM the relationship. The relationship is made out of only two parts. I am 50%. This means that I have a lot more agency than sitting on the sidelines feeling confused. It means that I have a lot more power to make of this relationship something that helps me navigate life. It means that at the very least I hold half the answers. I stop being confused the moment I realize I own this thing, and as such, I get to decide. I stop looking to the other person for answers and start outlining what it is I need to survive (respect, trust) and what it is I need to thrive (an ally, joy.) I begin to realize that all I can do is communicate clearly about these things I need. I will either get them or I won't. What I decide to do if I do not have what I need is 100% up to me.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What happens when your partner doesn't see the value in you and continuously hurts you by searching for something in others knowing it hurts you?
Answer: What happens? In one scenario, I stay with this partner, wonder why he doesn’t love me, and begin living in a world of my creation where I believe that, unfortunately, I am not worth loving. I believe this non-love is the best I can do and spend all my time and energy attempting to preserve the very thing that causes me pain. There is another scenario: If my “partner” didn’t see value in me and hurt me searching for something in others, I would remind myself that I cannot change people, “make them see” or “make them love me”. “Making someone love me” is the most painful, most fruitless of efforts, because love cannot be manufactured in this way. I would ask myself why I consider it worth my time to be with someone who does not find me valuable. Identifying this answer will over time protect me from finding myself in this same predicament over and over. I would realize that it’s not my partner who is hurting me. I am hurting myself, by agreeing to stay with someone who is looking for something he is not finding in me. I would leave this partner to grant him full freedom to go find whatever he is looking for and spend the time and energy that I put into that relationship getting to know myself. What I would find is someone flawed and worthy of love. I would work hard at only being interested in people who are equally interested in me.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Why does my boyfriend always make himself the victim even when I was the one that got hurt first?
Answer: Here is something that has helped me with every one of my relationships: it’s possible for two people to be hurt. It’s possible for two people to be right. It’s possible for two people to have different perspectives, and have each one be valid - even if they seem contradictory. This shifts the goal. Things go from “I was first” or “it’s his fault” or “I am right” to “we have to understand each other better”. The goal becomes figuring things out, so that we are both acting in the interest of the relationship, rather than our own. Of course this is really hard, in particular when I feel hurt. So, I try to set myself aside. Not permanently. Just long enough to listen to the other person and really truly put myself in their shoes. Then I say something like “I can absolutely see why you did what you did.” Then, I represent myself and my perspective. The result is less about victims and who wins the argument and who got hurt more - and more about feeling safe and loved despite our shortcomings. More like feeling we are building something together. Maybe something that will withstand not just our inevitable mistakes but also a wild, unpredictable life that we are now attempting to live together.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What should I do if my partner doesn't love me the way I want despite mentioning it multiple times?
Answer: If my partner doesn’t love me the way that I want, I have two options. The first option is to feel that being loved in many different ways and not just in the way that I want to be loved is a sign of abundance and good fortune. I don’t want to miss any love, and the shape it comes in matters less to me than the fact that someone wonderful wants to give it to me. In this case I accept that people love me the way they love me, not the way I want them to. I accept their love the way it is. Because, you cannot change other people, and cannot change the way they love. The second option is to feel I don’t want this love in the way it’s presented to me. This means this person and their love and I are not compatible. Or, not good for each other. If the first option, where I accept the love in the form that it is given, is, for whatever reason, unavailable to me, the only other option is to go.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What motivates you to be an author?
Answer: I don’t think the motivation has ever been “I want to be an author”. What I feel instead is that I want to think about something. Or process something. Or express something. Or share something. I start putting it into words in my head and then feel an urge to write the words down as a way to not lose them. The fact that I am an author is a fortunate consequence of the fact that what I want is to write.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I feel down/depressed (bride) days before the wedding. Is this normal?
Answer: Everyone kept telling me that planning a wedding was “one of the best times of my life” and all I felt was stressed, anxious and sad. Sometimes, I even felt angry. A wedding has so many elements that can set off anxiety and depression: it’s highly emotional, not just for me but for people around me. It comes with a sense that I need to control everything. There are extremely high expectations from everyone important to me. There is pressure to make sure everything is perfect. I realize I am living in an ever present sense of overwhelm. A wedding is a bit like New Year’s day, where happiness is forced and obligatory - only deeply personal, and with everyone you love in the same room. Of course it’s normal to feel down. I used my angst as an opportunity to ask myself so many important questions. Are my future husband and I able to talk about how we feel? Is this what I want, or what others want? Am I taking care of myself? Might I step away from wedding planning to reconnect to the person I am going to marry? It helped me to understand that a wedding implies change, and change is loss, even when it’s good. What I felt had a name I did not expect came with a wedding: grief. You grieve the life you used to have, to make room for the life you are building.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What key advice do you have for caring for a loved one with dementia?
Answer: Caring for someone with dementia is completely, utterly, hopelessly overwhelming. If I am not dedicated to taking care of myself, it cannot be done. Taking care of myself involves making sure I am getting enough sleep, eating well and exercising. It means I am able to take breaks, and that I have people to talk to - friends, a support group, a therapist (ideally all three.) It means I have a way to spend time doing other things, grounding things, that remind me what “normal” feels like, because dealing with a person with dementia will make me feel like I don’t know what is real. If I don’t take care of myself, if it makes me feel selfish or if I decide it’s not important, I will buckle under the pressure of how impossible it is to care for someone who cannot care for themselves.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What should I do if I originally agreed to sleep with this guy, but I recently changed my mind about it? I feel like I deserve better than spending the night with a guy that I barely know at an Airbnb, instead of going out on a actual first date.
Answer: The best thing I can do for my relationships, and for me, is to express what I want as clearly as possible. And, because I am human, what I want can change. And, I can change my mind. I can say, for example, that I want pizza for dinner and then on my way to the restaurant feel like eating something else. I can say I feel like going dancing, and then say I’d rather watch a movie. This happens to all of us every day: what we want changes, and the better we express it, the better we represent ourselves, the better others can understand us. If I tell someone I agree to sleep with them, I can absolutely change my mind. I can say “I originally agreed to sleep with you, but I’ve changed my mind” and then watch his reaction closely. An ideal reaction might be “that sounds great - what would you like to do instead?” or even “I feel disappointed, but I understand.” If instead he says “you can’t go back on what we agreed to” or “now you have to sleep with me because that’s we said we’d do” that is someone I want nothing to do with.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What is a human being's deepest emotional need?
Answer: Safety, refuge. A freedom from feeling I am in danger or that I have to defend myself. Belonging. Feeling like I fit in. Peace. Living in a state of harmony. Connection. Having deep rich relationships, including one with me. Sovereignty. Making my own choices. Purpose. I dedicate myself to something meaningful. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Is the Acropolis, Athens, Greece worth a trip?
Answer: The Acropolis in Athens is absolutely breathtaking and is worth traveling across the world to see it. I mean, look at it: Beyond the acropolis, Athens is absolutely fabulous: warm, beautiful, peaceful, livable and full of personality, plus what I consider to be some of the most delicious food in the world.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What is the difference between forgiving and forgetting?
Answer: Forgive: the absence of resentment or ill will. Forget: the absence of remembering.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My girlfriend is moving to a different country. I feel like she will ditch me for someone better. Should I break up with her?
Answer: To determine if what I am doing is the right life strategy, I multiply it. What happens if I repeatedly leave people before they can leave me? I never let down my guard. I never know intimacy. I never trust, and cannot be trusted. I never learn how to express what I want, how to have a difficult conversation, how to create sturdy relationships. I end up isolated, lonely, in pain. The very pain I was sure I was avoiding by leaving first. Conclusion: this is not the right life strategy. It’s maladaptive, ensures I miss everything that is beautiful, ensures I cause the very things I fear. What happens if instead I communicate clearly, love with my whole heart, remind myself pain cannot be avoided, so I might as well give myself fully? I definitely suffer from heartbreak. I can’t escape this. But also, I live with courage, know intimacy, create relationships that are real and deep. Each relationship teaches me about relationships so that I get better at life’s most important skill. And, I improve the relationship with myself: instead of being someone who robs me, who sabotages me, I become someone I can count on - and someone I am certain is worth loving.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My girlfriend told me that she wants to move in with me. I have my own apartment and I like my peace and quiet, but I also love her. We've been together for a year now. What should I do?
Answer: Ah, yes. It’s customary to meet someone and eventually move in with them. Customary means “according to custom” but it does not mean “mandatory.” Just because something works for everyone does not mean it’s what works for me. I can design my own life and decide what works for me and what I need to give the best of me to others. Moving in (or deciding not to) is not just your life but your partner’s life too, so the most important thing to do is talk about it, and talk about it a lot. “I love you, and am very committed to us, but need my own space” can be difficult because many people confuse it with “I don’t love you enough to move in with you” and moving in and love are not related. It’s also important to consider that what you want might change - or might be flexible. You might not want to move in now but might feel differently in a year; or, you might be open to moving in if you can find a place where you can have your own space. When I met my current partner, I told him early on (date one) that I was a very committed person, but really valued my own space. We have now been together four years and live separately. We talk about the possibility of someday moving into a place where we might each have our own space, but have agreed we are not in a rush. In the beginning this was a source of tension, but over time he has come to really appreciate the fact that, to us, we have the best of both worlds: the ability to be together when we want (he stays over often) and the ability to have our own peace and quiet. Please, listen closely to what you need. Communicate as clearly and as honestly as possible. And know that the way to happiness is to design your own life, in accordance with your own needs. Never confuse “customary” with something you have to do.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My ex-father-in-law left me his Bentley in his will. My ex-wife wants me to give it to her because she said her dad forgot to change his will after our divorce. What should I do?
Answer: Many years ago I dated a guy who gave me a ring that belonged to his mother. It was not an engagement ring, but it was a family heirloom. What he intended with the gift was to show his commitment, material representation that I was important to him and that he was playing the long game. In a sense, he had not given me the ring - he had given it to the woman he was with. When we broke up, I did not for a moment consider keeping it. For him, the ring meant something. Family. History. The passage of time. His life story. For me, the ring was valuable, and beautiful, but it was just a ring. It did not belong to me.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: The guy I’m talking to made it clear that if we were to continue and get more serious, I would have to give up concerts for the rest of my life in order to be a respectful wife. Do I comply or move on?
Answer: Attempting to control another person’s behavior (here is what you can and can’t do) is a sign. Isolating someone from people they love or things they like doing (you cannot go to concerts) is a sign. Acting possessive (you are mine) is sign. Expecting unrealistic things (you have to give up something) is a sign. A sign of what, you may ask? These things are not a sign of love - they are behavior typical of someone who is or will become an abuser. Relationships don’t require “compliance”. They don’t require subservience. They don’t require obedience or deference or submissiveness. People who love me in a way that is healthy do not want to control me or own me or treat me like I am property. What they want is to get to know me and support me and maybe, if we are lucky, to grow with me.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My fiance forbids my gay friend from attending the wedding. What should I do?
Answer: What a word. “Forbid.” It’s a command, hindering, deprivation. It is such a stark contrast with “fiancé”, which is promise, support, a future, your team. And the word is in reference to you, and a friend. You are ushering someone into your life and your future who wants to separate you from your friend, isolating you, instead of doing what he should which is promoting friendships and wanting more people to love you. And the reason - because your friend is gay? Think about what you want for yourself, and for your life, and for your future. Think about what you want to create. What do you want more of? What do you want your life to look like? Do you want sunlight, or do you want a dungeon? Because, he is showing you the blueprint. You are working with the locksmith, the master designing the key.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My boyfriend has a girl best friend that he used to like. What should I do?
Answer: Ugh. I know what you mean. My boyfriend has girl friends he used to like, really beautiful ex-girlfriends that are also interesting people, and an ex he was married to that he had two beautiful children with. Regrettably, there is only one course of action that I have broken down into the following steps: To remember with both clarity and ferocity that I am supremely worth loving. To accept. Accept that this man had a life before I met him. Accept that this life is precisely what shaped him into the person I love. To be grateful to all the beautiful women who came before me for all the things he learned that today make him a most excellent life companion. (And maybe sometimes to glare at him because how dare he.)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My boyfriend at times doesn't want me to touch his body, but later he will say “oh, go ahead you can touch me”, then he expects me not to be upset. Why?
Answer: My body belongs to me. Like pretty much every other body, sometimes she wants to be touched and sometimes she doesn’t. Sometimes I ask my boyfriend to hold me tight and sometimes I ask him not to touch me. He does the same with me. The fact that we express what we want clearly and directly (when it comes to things the other can’t possibly just know) ensures we understand what each other’s boundaries are, so we can respect and honor them.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My boyfriend prioritizes a competitive MMA event with his friends over going with me getting my first tattoo. He is trying to make time but his friends are being determined. Now he fears upsetting his friends. What should I do?
Answer: When my boyfriend wants to spend time with his friends doing whatever, I have two choices: The first: To regard his time with his friends as something in direct conflict with time with me. To feel he is choosing them over me. To feel he is not making me his priority. This first choice is painful, tense, constricting, full of resentment, unsustainable, a dead end. The second: To rejoice in the fact that he has a whole life that does not include me, which makes the time he spends with me richer and healthier. To support him in everything he does, with my whole heart. To make whatever he wants to do easier, rather than harder. You have plans with friends? I can just rebook what we had planned - or, you can go with your friends and I can go with mine. If I have something in my hands that is precious to me, I hold it loosely. If I tighten my hand to grip it, to keep it close, to make it mine, I strangle it, suffocate it, take away its space and its air. I want it to have room to move, to breathe, to live, which in turn gives me the room to do the same.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I resist the temptation of binge-watching Netflix and instead do something productive… like folding laundry! 😴👖?
Answer: Whenever I find myself in a predicament like this, I use a timer. I set it for 10 minutes. 10 minutes to do “something productive” for every hour of whatever is tempting me. I set the timer. I fold for ten minutes. When the timer goes off, I am free. I watch something for an hour. I set the timer for ten minutes. At the end of the day (or the weekend) my clothes are folded, my place in order, and I feel I got the time I needed to do what I wanted to do - watch a show, nap, read, or whatever it was that I considered a temptation. You would be surprised at how much can be done in 10 minutes - even more in ten minute increments.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: If you hurt someone over 40 years ago and you have always wanted to apologize to them, should you? It has bothered me, and I am truly sorry for my choices in life.
Answer: Decades ago, I went through a bad breakup and reacted in a way I later regretted. For years I dreamed about apologizing - both while I was awake, daydreaming, and while I slept. I had recurring, angsty dreams about seeing him at a distance and walking over to him to apologize, then being unable to find him. In those dreams I moved towards him, threading through crowded rooms; I walked down streets, only to turn a corner and find that he had vanished. One day, I reached out to a common friend. “Hey” I said. “The last time I saw Edward we were going through a terrible breakup. I want to apologize for the way I handled it, but don’t want to reach out to him if it would cause him discomfort or any form of distress. Do you think you can tell him I reached out to you, and intend to call him if he is open to it? Our friend got back to me a couple of days later. “He would be so thrilled to hear from you” he said. So, I called him. The first thing out of my mouth was “I deeply regret what I did and what I said. I am so very sorry. You were extremely important to me and I think of you all the time. Thank you for the role you played in shaping who I am today.” “Dushka” he said. “I forgave you instantly. We were so young and what I did to you was awful. I too think of you all the time and also regret how terribly things ended between us.” We proceeded to have a long conversation, reminisced, and updated each other on so many things we wondered about when we were kids. “You always asked if I’d grow up and forget you” I said. “I have not forgotten.” I cannot tell you the peace I felt when I got off the phone - like something I had left undone was finally taken care of. We agreed we’d do everything possible to see each other before the end of that year, and he died, a tragic, early, unexpected death, a few months later. In my dreams I sometimes see him sitting in a chair at the end of a long room, smiling at me. If there is something you feel you need to do, do it (after confirming that doing so would not cause the other person harm.) Making amends is a gift, and we very rarely have as much time as we think. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Is taking revenge on someone who cheated on you okay?
Answer: Taking revenge on someone who cheated on me means I loved someone and gave them my time, my trust and my heart and they took it all and hurt me. Then, in the name of revenge, I react by taking more of my time and give them all my attention and my thoughts. Hmmm. No thank you. If someone hurts me, I am so better off giving my most precious resources to someone who deserves them: I can instead give them to me, and use them to heal, to love me, and to move on.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: My boss threatened to fire me. Should I give him a 2 week notice now that I got a new job?
Answer: How you treat people will follow you everywhere. A job connects to another in unexpected ways, across industries and across borders. And, time has a way of changing your perspective of what happened. Be as correct as you can. Give a full two weeks notice in writing, and add that you are grateful for the opportunity that you were given. Treat people well and with respect, even if they treated you poorly. Don’t let poor treatment diminish you. Poor treatment of you is on the other person - it’s not on you. There is a saying - “watch where you walk because one day you will have to pick up every step.” Make the weight of the steps that you pick up light. You will be so happy that you did.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I love someone who doesn't love me back, but I think he does but just didn't realise it. What do I do in this case?
Answer: I spent so much time making excuses for others and justifying others and adjusting reality to fit what I wanted to be true. It’s not that he doesn’t love me - it’s that he doesn’t know it. That he doesn’t know how to express it. That he doesn’t know yet how compatible we are - if only he could see. If only he could see me. I will get him to love me. I would sink days, weeks, months, years. And when the swirl of my effort receded I was left with - well. He said all along he did not love me and I chose not to listen. It’s not that he’s a heartbreaker. I am the heartbreaker. I did this to myself. I now believe that if someone loves me it’s their responsibility to know it, to want it and to express it. I will show up in the same way: I know what I want and what I want is you. Relationships are hard enough. The least I can ask for is a basic level of relationship competence, and clarity.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I told my boss that I'm going to resign, and he offered me twice my current salary if I stay, what should I do?
Answer: If my boss offered to double my salary as a result of me saying I was leaving, I would realize that he has been deliberately underpaying me all along. If I am worth double what you have been paying me, why didn’t you pay me what I deserved from the beginning? To me, this betrays a culture where good work is not appreciated, and probably means I will not be getting a raise or a promotion the next time one was due. In a culture where someone would be willing to double my salary as a result of me saying I was going to leave, leaving would be seen as an absence of loyalty. I would be worried about staying in a place where I am not trusted. What was it that you were planning to do after resigning? Did it involve something less familiar? What do you think would be better for you - something you know how to do, or something new that is likely to challenge you? And now for the most salient question. What was it that made you want to resign? Have you considered that whatever made you unhappy will remain exactly the same, unless you loved everything about your job except for the salary?

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I think my boyfriend got upset with me because I didn't pay attention to him. I know he's upset, but he said "fine". What do I have to do to fix this?
Answer: It’s my job and my responsibility to clearly spell out for others what I want and what I need. It’s unreasonable for me to expect others to guess, to infer or to intuit anything I might be expecting, wishing or assuming others will do. Along the same vein, it is not my job to somehow figure out why another person might be upset. If I ask “is everything OK?” and they say “fine,” my work is done. I do not have extrasensory perception. The expectation that someone will do for us something we have not asked for, or that someone will guess why we are upset without us having to explain it is unreasonable and even toxic. Learning to communicate clearly and with compassion is essential to healthy relationships - and to not burdening ourselves with attempting to do that which cannot be done.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What do you do when you realize that you are the problem?
Answer: Less blame, more responsibility. Less avoiding, more communication. Less lies, more accountability. Less indignance, more “I am sorry.” Less manipulation, more clarity. Less flaking, more reliability. Less resentment, more boundaries. Less roller coasters, more stability. Less criticizing, more listening. Less judging, more accepting. Less taking, more giving. Less self-criticism, more self compassion. Less disquiet, more self care.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: What is the difference between self concept, self awareness, self esteem, self confidence, and self control with examples?
Answer: Self-concept: How I see myself. Example: I think I am kind. Self-awareness: My ability to truly see myself. Example: I can recognize my patterns. Self-esteem: The regard with which I hold myself. Example: I am able to say no. Self-confidence: My ability to believe in myself. Example: I can't do that now, but I believe I can learn. Self-control: An ability to exercise restraint, discipline. Example: Just because I want it doesn’t mean I have to have it.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Am I overthinking my relationship, or is it intuition?
Answer: For me, overthinking is obsessive, repetitive, circular, unproductive, compulsive. I can’t stop, it’s the same thought over and over, and it doesn’t get me anywhere, like a tiger, prowling around and a round in a small enclosure. If true thought is a river, overthinking is a puddle. Intuition is more in my body than in my mind. It presents itself as a feeling rather than a sentence. It feels like light, or like dread. It feels eager or clear or like an iron sheet that is dropped right in front of me. It’s much easier to put it into immediate action. If overthinking is a puddle, intuition is lightning. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Do you agree when people say stop letting your brain play mind games with you, they are wrong because your brain is usually correct on what you can or cannot do? Do you think your brain is more honest than the people who care about you?
Answer: I have to work hard every day at not believing everything I think, because my brain most definitely plays tricks on me. Two every day, simple examples of this are my expectations and my assumptions. Expectations lead to my own disappointment, and assumptions have me believing that you think what I think you think, instead of what you actually think. I mean, think about that. Another example is how I react when someone I’m into doesn’t text me back. Clearly this means they don't care about me anymore, right? Except, a person’s reasons to not text me back are often not even related to me. How many times does my brain believe that things that have nothing to do with me are about me? What about when I am convinced another person is responsible for my happiness? Or when I think I’m bad at something, just because I have never tried it before? Or when I am convinced I am right just because I am angry? Or when I believe a feeling will last forever, when nothing is more fleeting? What about when I believe others have to change to accommodate my feelings? (I am sorry to inform you I need you to stop seeing other people, so I can manage my jealousy.) What about when we meet a person and feel like we know who they are? Or, when we believe that bad things cannot happen to good people? What about all the times we believe we can’t, when really we can? What about all the conclusions we jump to because we are biased, or prejudiced? What about the times we believe that the rules that apply to everyone apply to everyone but us? When we believe something can happen to other people but not to us? Or in another place, but not here? What about the times we believe our perspective is the only perspective, and if I am right this means you are wrong? What about all the times I assume others think like I think? What about the times I want something that is familiar, even though unfamiliar can be a lot better? What about my inner voice, which lives convinced that berating me will get me to change my behavior, and I berate myself for years despite the fact it has never worked? What about me believing that I can do many things at the same time? Or many things in a short span of time? There is a lot of science behind the many ways our brains play tricks on us. There is a name for these: cognitive distortions. The more I know about them, the better I get at identifying when my brain is just trying to get me to do what she wants. I know you are making me feel anxious with all your catastrophic thoughts. I don’t think the outcome will be as bad as you want me to think.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do I know if I'm over a bad breakup?
Answer: You wake up looking forward to the day rather than feeling a hole in your stomach. Thinking about them feels like a memory, not an obsession. It feels nostalgic, not compulsive. You remember, and remembering makes you smile. It does not feel painful. You feel grateful for what you had. You feel grateful for what you learned. You don't even think about doing forensic social media searches. You feel an absence of bitterness and resentment. The idea of meeting someone new sounds appealing rather than horrifying or overwhelming. Sometimes, you need perspective and they are who you call. When you begin a new relationship, you know you are better at relationships because of what you went through with them.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Should your parents do everything for you? Why or why not?
Answer: If my parents do everything for me, how will I learn that things don’t just resolve themselves? How will I learn about responsibility? How will I learn that I can rely on myself? How do I learn about the value of work? How do I become confident, if I don't get to show me what I can do? How do I learn to manage my time? How do I learn to manage my frustration? How do I learn to manage difficulty? How will I understand the dedication and work it takes to do certain things? How can I value what others do for me if to my eyes it happens magically? How do I learn to feed myself, do my laundry? The more my parents do for me, the more I will suffer later. The more they do for me, the harder it will be for me to become an adult. A parent’s job is to prepare their kid for the world. If they do everything for me, how will I learn to get by without them?

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: Is it ever a good idea to get back together with someone who broke your heart?
Answer: Who is this person who broke my heart? How did they do it? What it circumstance, or was it character? Did the heartbreak involve deceit or betrayal? Was the decision one sided, or mutual? Was it related to a big decision, such as living far away? Was it an absence of compatibility? After we parted ways, how did we behave, with ourselves and with each other? Did we show respect and care for one another, was there regard or friendship; were we hurtful, was ghosting involved? And, when I say “this person broke my heart” am I clear on the role that I played? For example, did this person show me something that I refused to see, tell me something I refused to hear? In other words, did they really break my heart or did I break my own heart? And, what did we learn? Have we changed? If two people get together and break up and get back together without anything having changed, then we are just watching a rerun, and we already know how it ends. (Drawing by Dan Roam)

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: How do your parents know everything about you?
Answer: I have been dating my current partner for four years. In that time he has changed a lot - he is today a very different person from the person I once met. I have loved being a witness to this change. I’ve loved listening, asking questions and noticing all the things he does. Wow. You are a sponge. I’ve love noting the presence of certain behaviors across everything he spends time on. He is dedicated, and wholehearted. He never does anything halfway. Everything intrigues him, which explains how he knows so much about so many things. In the course of my life I’ve learned how fragile love is. People throw around “forever and ever” and swear they will always love you but the fact is you lose someone’s love over nothing, and this can happen any time. I’ve decided that the only thing I can do is love well, and that the best I can do is give another person my full attention. Instead of taking for granted I know him, because we’ve been dating for four years, I remind myself I don't know him at all and try to remain deeply curious about this person I share my life with. Who are you, and why did you appear when you did? Do you remember you did that thing? What a departure to how you handle that now. If a grown man can change that much, can you imagine a baby, who turns into a toddler, who turns into a child, who turns into a pre-teen, a teenager? Every day they take in enough to assemble an evolving universe. Parents know us because they made us and because they see us every day. But, how much do they miss? How many times do they assume they know us and don’t realize they had to start over, get to know us again and again? I am not who you think I am. I never was. I think you confused me with you and instead I am my own person. I don’t think it’s possible for anyone to know everything about anyone. Not even a doting parent. Not even an ardent lover. I don’t think we even know everything about ourselves.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: If you have friends that don't take the time out to see you or even talk to you, should you still keep them in your life?
Answer: I really appreciate the friends I have who make it a point to give me their time. But, you know what? I also have good friends I don’t see very often. I recognize they are really busy. It’s not that they don’t take time to see me - it’s that it has nothing to do with me. Their lives are overwhelmed and when we hang out, maybe once or twice a year, it’s delightful. I also have friends that just don’t think of me that often (and to be fair, neither do I.) I don’t really have to decide if I keep them or don’t keep them in my life - they are not really in it. But, when they graze it - say, when we run into each other - I’m happy it happened. It takes something directed and damaging for me to keep someone out of my life. Time is too short for unnecessary strife. Different circumstances, related answer:

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I’m a 17-year-old guy in a new neighborhood and a girl about my age lives not too many doors away. How do I talk to her, not even in a romantic way but in general as people scare me, especially girls?
Answer: There is one way to be less scared of people, and less scared of talking to them, and that is practice. Practice by keeping the stakes really low. Practice by just saying “hello” or “good morning” or “good afternoon”. It’s just a greeting. Talk to people as you move through your day. You don’t have to say much. You are just practicing the act of interaction. Some people will react in a way that is friendly and open and others will be standoffish - and the way people react is related to the day they are having or what they are carrying inside of them and not to you. Knowing this separates you from their reaction: it’s not about me. It’s not “rejection”. It’s a reflection of where they are at. The more you practice, the easier talking to others becomes. The more you practice, the more you realize we are all nervous, and all hungry for connection. There is a 50% chance the girl is wondering how on earth to talk to you. Make it easier for her. The more you practice, the more you see that people are people. Girls are people. Just say hello.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: I’ve been skipping the same class for the past 2 weeks. I don’t even have a bad grade but the anxiety of having to go back and the guilt is eating me alive. What do I do?
Answer: I’ve read so many fairy tales about brave knights who slay dragons. They are a metaphor, I think. We’re all knights, and the dragons we slay are inside us. I skipped class when I was in school. It started with a knot of anxiety - I didn’t do my homework. If the teacher calls on me, I won’t know. The more I skipped, the bigger the anxiety became, until I felt like it was eating me alive. My parents were sure I was skipping class to go on wild adventures, and there I was, hiding in the bathroom, terrified of my chemistry teacher. There is one way out (of the bathroom and of the prison of my own angst) and that is to face my anxiety. To say - however big you feel, you will get bigger tomorrow, so I might as well face you today. As you do this - face up to what makes you anxious instead of attempting to escape it - it will get smaller. What you are doing is practicing the act of addressing whatever scares you. A practice that will serve you well for the rest of your life. Go. Slay your dragon.

Name: Dushka Zapata
Question: "The only way to get rid of temptation is to yield to it". Do you agree?
Answer: In my experience, yielding to temptation is akin to feeding it. Feeding things is what makes them grow. If I want a cookie (a cookie being a cookie, or a metaphor for temptation), eating a cookie will make me want another cookie, rather than making me not want cookies. Here are things that help me manage this cookie-temptation: First, to better understand why I want this cookie. Am I eating enough? Am I hungry? Do I have pleasure in my life? Am I bored? Am I looking for comfort? Am I feeling lonely? Am I unhappy, dissatisfied? Wanting something is seldom about the thing I want. Plan around the cookie.
